questions.question: Infrared optical ______ can be used for measuring and monitoring temperatures and hot spots of jet engine rotor blades.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Pyrometer.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• A pyrometer__ is a sort of remote-sensing thermometer that measures the temperature of things that are far away.
 
• Pyrometers have appeared in many forms throughout history.
 
• It can be used for measuring and monitoring temperatures and hot spots of jet engine rotor blades.
 
• It is a device that determines the temperature of a surface from a distance based on the quantity of thermal radiation it produces, a process known as pyrometry and sometimes radiometry.
 
• The majority of pyrometers work by detecting radiation from the body being measured.
 
• It is founded on the idea that the intensity of light received by the observer is proportional to the distance between the observer and the distant source's temperature.
 
• A modern pyrometer consists of an optical system and a detector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• A hygrometer is a device that measures the amount of water vapour present in the air, soil, or restricted places.
 
• An ammeter is a device that measures the current flowing through a circuit.
 
• A Machmeter is a flight instrument in an aircraft's pitot-static system that displays the ratio of true airspeed to sound speed, a dimensionless quantity known as Mach number.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the Supreme Court of India come into existence after Independence?

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of India** is the country's highest judicial court, according to the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Supreme Court is established and constituted according to **Article 124.**

• The Supreme Court's strength has** increased from 30 to 34 **upon the appointment of the new four judges on September 18, 2019.

questions.question: An/A ______ is a finite set of instructions which, when followed, accomplish a particular task.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**algorithm.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• An **algorithm**__ is a finite set of instructions that, if followed, accomplishes a particular task.
 
• It is the step by step procedure for solving any problem.
 
• Algorithms are used to specify how calculations, data processing, automated reasoning, automated decision-making, and other tasks should be carried out.
 
• All algorithms must meet the following requirements:
 
 
• The **inputs** to an algorithm can be zero or more and come from a specific set of objects.
 
• An algorithm has one or more **outputs** that are related to the inputs in some way.
 
• Each step must be properly stated, and each instruction must be concise and clear.
 
• After a **finite number of steps**, the algorithm must always end.
 
• All operations must be sufficiently fundamental to be completed** precisely **and in a finite amount of time.

questions.question: With which of the following banks has the Government of India signed a $500 million project to build safe and green national highway corridors in Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh?

__
 
• The Indian government and the **World Bank__** signed a $500 million agreement to create safe and environmentally friendly national highway corridors in Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The project will also help the **Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH)** improve its ability to mainstream safety and green technologies.
 
• On behalf of the Indian government, Dr C S Mohapatra, Additional Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, and Sumila Gulyani, Acting Country Director, India, signed the agreement.
 
• The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) loan, worth $500 million, has a maturity of** 18.5 years**, with a five-year grace period.
 
• The Green National Roadways Corridors Project will help MoRTH build 783 km of highways across a variety of geographies by incorporating safe and green technology designs including local and marginal materials, industrial byproducts, and other bioengineering solutions.
 
• The initiative will aid in the reduction of GHG(greenhouse gas ) emissions from highway building and maintenance.
 
• The chosen stretches in **Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Himachal Pradesh** would also assist in improving connectivity and promoting economic development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

questions.question: Trachoma is a preventable disease that results from poor hygiene and sanitation. Which of the following body parts does it affect?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Eye.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Trachoma is a preventable disease that results from poor hygiene and sanitation.
 
• Trachoma is a disease of the **eye**__ caused by the Chlamydia trachomatis bacteria.
 
• Trachoma causes **irreversible blindness.**
 
• It is a public health issue in 44 nations, causing around 1.9 million individuals to become blind or visually impaired.
 
• 137 million people live in trachoma-endemic areas and are in danger of trachoma blindness, according to data from March 2020.
 
• The infection is spread through infected people's eye and nose discharges, which can be transmitted directly or indirectly.
 
• Trachoma causes about** 1.4% of all blindness worldwide.**
 
• Through an innovative, multi-faceted public health strategy known as **S.A.F.E**, the World Health Organization has set a goal of eliminating trachoma by 2020.
 
• Cataract also affects the human eyes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Carditis is a disease that affects the human **Heart.**
 
• Gastritis is a disease that affects the **Stomach.**
 
• Otitis is a disease that affects the **Ear.**

questions.question: Which of the following is the full form of ASCII?

options.text: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
Analytical Scientific Code for Information Interchange
Asian Standard Code for Information Interchange
Analytical Standard Code for Intermitted Information

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**American Standard Code for Information Interchange.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ASCII stands for **American Standard Code for Information Interchange.**__
 
• It's a standard data-transmission code used by smaller and less powerful computers to represent textual data (letters, numbers, and punctuation marks) as well as non-input-device commands (control characters).
 
• Like other coding systems, it turns data into **standardised digital formats** that let computers communicate with one another and process and store data more efficiently.
 
• The ASCII code was created for teletypewriters but has now found widespread use in personal computers.
 
• Seven-digit binary integers, or numbers made up of multiple sequences of** 0s and 1s**, are used in the standard ASCII coding.
 
• Because there are 128 different possible combinations of seven 0s and 1s, the code can represent **128 different characters.**
 
• A lowercase "p" is represented by the binary sequence 1110000, while an uppercase "P" is represented by the binary sequence 1010000.
 
• The seven information bits plus a **parity bit **(used for error-checking purposes or to represent special symbols) in ASCII code are usually placed in an eight-bit field.

questions.question: The polity of a country is designed according to its ______ and any change to the polity is possible only when an amendment is made.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Constitution.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The polity of a country is designed according to its **Constitution**__ and any change to the polity is possible only when an amendment is made.
 
• The Indian Constitution can be amended to meet the **changing demands of the country.**
 
• A constitution that can be very easily changed or amended is often called **flexible.**
 
• A constitution that is very difficult to amend is described as** rigid.**
 
• The Indian Constitution** combines both flexible and rigid characteristics.**
 
• When an amendment seeks to change an article relating to the** allocation of powers between the states and the federal government**, or an article relating to the representation, the States must be contacted and consented to.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• During its 74-year existence, the Soviet Union had four constitutions (**1918, 1924, 1936, and 1977**).
 
• The Communist Party of the Soviet Union's control ended in 1991, and the Soviet Union rapidly collapsed.
 
• In 1993, the newly formed Russian Federation adopted a new constitution as a result of this political upheaval.

questions.question: Kolhapur city is located on the banks of which of the following rivers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Panchganga.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kolhapur** is a city in the Indian state of Maharashtra.
 
• It is located on the banks of river **Panchganga.**__
 
• Because of its spiritual history and the antiquity of its shrine Mahalaxmi, Kolhapur is known as '**Dakshin Kashi**' or Kashi of the South.
 
• Kolhapur is famed for its hand-crafted and braided leather slippers known as Kolhapuri chappal, which was awarded **Geographical Indication status in 2019.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• The **Panchganga River**__, located in Maharashtra, is one of India's most important rivers.
 
• It is a major tributary of the **Krishna River**, joining it at Narsobawadi.
 
• It flows through the borders of Kolhapur city.
 
• It originates from** Prayag Sangam.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The** Sarayu** is a river in Uttarakhand, India, that originates on a ridge south of the Nanda Kot mountain.

 
 
• The river is mentioned several times in the Ramayana, an ancient Indian epic.
 
• It flows through the Kumaon Himalayas, passing past the cities of Kapkot, Bageshwar, and Seraghat on its way to Pancheshwar, where it joins the Sharda River.
 
 
 
• The **Chambal River **is a tributary of the Yamuna River.
 
 
• The river forms the boundary between Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh before turning southeast to join the Yamuna in Uttar Pradesh state.
 
 
 
• **Musi River **is a tributary of the Krishna River in the Deccan Plateau.
 
 
• It flows through Telangana state in India.
 
• The river originates in Ananthagiri Hills near Vikarabad in Telangana.

questions.question: In which of the following states/union territories is India’s highest Meteorological Centre situated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ladakh.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• India’s highest Meteorological Centre is situated in** Ladakh__.**
 
• It is located at **3,500 metres** above sea level in Leh.
 
• **Dr Harsh Vardhan**, Minister of Earth Sciences (MoES), virtually inaugurated the centre.
 
• The Leh centre is the second Meteorological Centre in the Himalayas, after** Itanagar in Arunachal Pradesh.**
 
• It would give localised weather predictions and early warnings for the Union Territory's Leh and Kargil districts, as well as various tourist destinations.
 
• All stakeholders will receive regular updates from the new meteorological centre, which will provide weather forecasts for short (3 days), medium (12 days), and long (1 month) periods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The India Meteorological Department (IMD) intends to set up ten Automatic Weather Stations (AWS) in key sites such as **Drass, Kargil, Pangong Tso, Zanskar Valley, and Nubra Valley.**
 
• Currently, India has **28 meteorological centres **located throughout the country.
 
• The India Meteorological Department (IMD), the country's primary agency for meteorological observations and forecasting, relies on these centres to deliver accurate and timely weather-related information.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Supreme Court set up in Calcutta by the East India Company?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1773.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Supreme Court was set up in Calcutta by the East India Company in **1773.**__
 
• The King of England's Regulating Act of 1773 cleared the stage for the formation of the **Supreme Court of Judicature in Calcutta.**
 
• On March 26,** 1774**, Letters of Patent were issued to establish the Supreme Court of Judicature at Calcutta.
 
• It was established as a Court of Record, with full power and authority to hear and determine all complaints about any crimes, as well as to entertain, hear, and determine any suits or actions brought against any of His Majesty's subjects in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa(present-day Odisha).
 
• **King George – III **founded the Supreme Courts of Madras and Bombay on December 26, 1800, and December 8, 1823, respectively.
 
• The Constitution of India was enacted on **January 26, 1950**, after India gained independence in 1947.
 
• The Supreme Court of India was also established, with its inaugural meeting on** January 28, 1950**.
 
• The Supreme Court is established and constituted according to **Article 124.**
 
• The Supreme Court is the highest court in the country's judicial system.
 
• It is located in Tilak Marg,** New Delhi.**
